decision_rule: Start from each sealed fix and search backward independently.

Accept an exact subject only when its patch delta is causally material, it is in the fix ancestry, its parent-versus-subject counterfactual closes, and the exact subject has affirmative AI-attribution evidence.
A nearby AI-attributed commit is not accepted when its parent is already vulnerable and its delta does not create or complete the reviewed defect.
Use UNKNOWN rather than inferring AI attribution from coding style, chronology, repository-level AI activity, or a non-ancestor branch object.

blindness_attestation.notes: Public advisory metadata was used only to confirm the three named input surfaces for the third case; causal decisions were made from local Git objects and parent-versus-subject diffs.

squash_and_carrier_policy.rule: Prefer the landed exact commit that is an ancestor of the fix and whose own delta satisfies the causal counterfactual. Do not substitute recoverable atomic branch commits that are not in the fix ancestry.

cases.mechanism: Unauthenticated callers could reach both passkey registration endpoints, persist an attacker-controlled credential, authenticate that credential, and receive an administrator JWT. The fix removes registration from public-prefix allowlists, adds an explicit administrator guard at both registration controller entries, and rate-limits registration.

rejected_candidates.patch_and_counterfactual: The parent has no passkey surface. This commit adds registration option generation, registration verification, and credential persistence without an administrator guard; the default non-visitor configuration permits anonymous reachability.

ai_attribution.evidence: The raw commit has a human author, a one-line feature subject, no AI trailer, and no Git note.

rejected_candidates.patch_and_counterfactual: The parent can verify passkeys but returns only a success boolean. This commit signs role=admin JWTs for every successfully verified passkey, returns the token, and installs Bearer-token authentication, completing the registration-to-admin composition.

ai_attribution.evidence: The raw commit has a human author, no AI trailer or AI identity, and no Git note.

rejected_candidates.patch_and_counterfactual: The commit replaces substring checks with normalized exact/prefix matching but deliberately keeps both registration prefixes public. Its parent already exposes exact registration paths, so parent and subject are both vulnerable to the reviewed authorization defect.

cases.unknown_reason: The exact causal origin and privilege-escalation finalizer are both in the fix ancestry but lack affirmative AI attribution. The nearest AI-attributed ancestor preserves an already-existing public registration exemption and therefore fails the causal counterfactual.
cases.claim_boundary: This is UNKNOWN for AI-attributed causal origin, not UNKNOWN for the vulnerability mechanism or its human-authored causal chain.

fix.subject: Fix startup policy state mismatch — apply full merged rules after ES client starts

cases.mechanism: At startup the interactor contains only the compile-time baseline policy. The merged-policy update runs before the Endpoint Security client exists and returns at guard let client, while adapter.start(initialRules:) updates only mute prefixes. Managed and user rules therefore never reach the interactor until a later resync; uncovered paths take the explicit noRuleApplies default-allow branch. The fix moves policy application after adapter.start().

accepted_subjects.subject: Merge daemon into opfilter as single privileged process
accepted_subjects.patch_evidence: The commit deletes the daemon-to-filter XPC policy-push path and creates an in-process XPCServer whose initializer immediately invokes applyPolicyToFilter(). In the same commit, main constructs that server before calling adapter.start(), and ESInboundAdapter.updatePolicy() returns while its client is nil.
accepted_subjects.counterfactual_evidence: The parent retains a post-start callback path: the daemon pushes merged policy when the filter registers, and the filter callback invokes adapter.updatePolicy after its ES client has started. The subject removes that path and replaces it with a deterministic pre-start update that returns early; no autonomous post-start policy sync remains.

cases.claim_boundary: The confirmed security path is the inbound policy update. The fix message's broader claim that all three startup apply calls returned because of a nil client is not adopted: allowlist and jail state have different update behavior in the inspected source.

public_advisory_scope_confirmation.use: Scope confirmation only; origin decisions use local Git history.

cases.mechanism: Composite-action inputs were interpolated directly into generated Bash source, allowing shell metacharacters to execute in the action context. The fix moves prek-version and extra-args values into environment variables and constructs an argument array after validation.

accepted_subjects.subject: Add support for specifying prek-version (#7)
accepted_subjects.patch_evidence: The commit creates the prek-version input and inserts it directly into a composite Bash if condition and pip command. Those untrusted expression expansions execute as shell source.
accepted_subjects.counterfactual_evidence: The parent contains neither the prek-version input nor any inputs.prek-version interpolation. The subject introduces both the attacker-controlled surface and the executable shell sinks later removed by the fix.

accepted_subjects.subject: Rename `extra_args` to `extra-args` (#13)
accepted_subjects.patch_evidence: The commit adds the documented extra-args input and changes the Bash command to interpolate inputs.extra_args || inputs.extra-args directly. This adds the advisory's distinct kebab-case injection surface while preserving the legacy input.
accepted_subjects.counterfactual_evidence: The parent is already vulnerable through legacy inputs.extra_args but has no inputs.extra-args surface. The subject creates the new public alias and connects it to the same executable shell sink; removing this delta eliminates that advisory-listed surface while leaving the independently older legacy surface.

cases.claim_boundary: The legacy extra_args injection originates in an earlier non-AI initial commit. The second accepted AI subject is therefore a distinct surface-expanding compositional contributor, not the sole origin of the overall advisory. Non-ancestor pre-squash branch atomics were not substituted for the landed commits.
